title: Probationary / First 100 Shifts
summary: Become easy to trust: PPE/SCBA, hose, ladders, hydrant, radio, apparatus knowledge, and a reset after every run.

skills.title: Hose Advancement (Probation)
skills.summary: A short, correct attack-line evolution you can run on a quiet morning: pull, flake, charge, advance, reload.
skills.whyItMatters: Probation is where the company decides if you can be the backup firefighter without thinking.
learningPoints: Learn YOUR engine’s standard pull, not a generic academy story.
Flake so it can move. Pretty piles that trap the nozzle are wrong.
Talk to the operator: ready for water, kinks, shut down.
Reload is part of the skill. The next run is coming.
beforeYouDo: Ask which preconnect is first-due standard.
PPE as the company wears it for this drill.

terminology.meaning: Your usual probationary job on the line — feed hose, clear kinks, watch the nozzle.

safetyNotes: Charged lines knock people down. Body position.

drill.objective: Complete one standard attack-line pull to a door, charge, short advance, and a serviceable reload in the time your officer sets.
drill.equipment: Assigned engine, attack line, water if authorized, PPE.
drill.setup: Ask permission. Use tank water only if allowed. Safety for charged line.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Walk the bed and name the pull, the nozzle, and who calls for water.
debrief: Where are the kinks going to be?

15.title: 15-minute evolution
15.instructions: Pull, charge, advance 25 ft, shut, drain, reload. Officer watches backup work.
debrief: What would you do differently on stairs?

30.title: 30-minute two-reps + teaching
30.instructions: Two full evolutions, then you teach the next newer person (or talk it to the officer) to prove you know it.
debrief: Are you ready to be the backup at 0200?

readinessQuestions.q: On most engine companies the probationary firefighter on the line is primarily:
choices: Backup: hose, kinks, supporting the nozzle
readinessQuestions.why: Be excellent at the unglamorous job.

readinessQuestions.q: A reload that will not come off the bed next time:
If you are not sure this engine’s pull matches academy:
choices: Ask and then drill THIS bed

skills.title: PPE and SCBA Ready Check
skills.summary: Be dressed correctly, on air when required, with a partner check — every time, not only when someone is watching.
skills.whyItMatters: Companies notice who is still clipping a coat at the curb.
learningPoints: Your hooks and pockets should be the same every shift.
Buddy check is not optional because you are late.
Know how THIS pack turns on, not the academy rental.
After the run, gear comes back ready — not in a wet pile.
beforeYouDo: Issued gear and SCBA on the assigned seat.

terminology.meaning: Where you ride and which pack/tools are yours this shift.

safetyNotes: Cancer reduction: dirty gear is not a locker-room flex.

seeResources.label: SCBA Air Management Calculator
seeResources.note: Why the bottle is not ‘20 minutes of work.’

drill.objective: From the tones, complete a correct PPE/SCBA don and partner check, then reset the gear for the next run.
drill.setup: Do it in the bay. Officer or FTO watches interfaces.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Show where everything lives on your seat and name two interface fails.
debrief: Where is the spare hood?

15.title: 15-minute don/reset
15.instructions: Three dons. Third is timed only if the first two were correct. Reset after each.
debrief: Would you enter like this?

30.title: 30-minute work + air
30.instructions: Don, short work (stairs), gauge check, simulated low-air exit, full reset including cylinder policy.
commonMistakes: Leaving a used bottle for the next crew
debrief: What is our cylinder change rule?

readinessQuestions.q: A partner check is for:
choices: Every IDLH-ready don — including busy nights
readinessQuestions.why: You will not see your own open coat.

readinessQuestions.q: After a working fire, wet contaminated gear should be:
choices: Handled per department cancer/decon rules — not worn to the store
A badge of honor in the kitchen
Thrown on the apparatus seat forever
readinessQuestions.why: Probation is when habits lock in.

readinessQuestions.q: Your SCBA should be:
choices: The one assigned to your seat, checked at the start of shift
readinessQuestions.why: Start-of-shift check is a probationary essential.

skills.title: Apparatus Familiarity
skills.summary: Find the tool in the dark, explain what it is for, and put it back where the next person expects it.
skills.whyItMatters: ‘I don’t know this rig’ expires after about two shifts.
learningPoints: Inventory is a scavenger hunt with a standard.
Tools have a home. Inventing a new home creates missing tools.
Ask ‘when would we pull this?’ not just ‘what is this called.’
Know fuel, DEF, pump panel basics at a probationary level even if you are not the driver.
beforeYouDo: Assigned apparatus and the company’s inventory list if they have one.

terminology.meaning: Everything returns to the labeled place.

safetyNotes: Watch overhead doors, exhaust, and moving apparatus in the bay.
Do not start, pump, or drive unless you are authorized.

drill.objective: Locate ten assigned tools against a timer, state a use for each, and restore the compartments to service.
drill.setup: Do not remove equipment from service for a scavenger hunt if the company is the only in-service engine — use a training night.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Name the three tools you still cannot find. Go find them.
debrief: What is in the officer’s door?

15.title: 15-minute hunt
15.instructions: Officer names tools; you produce them and put them back.
debrief: What would we need for a car fire?

30.title: 30-minute teach-back
30.instructions: You give the next person a five-tool tour. Officer scores completeness.
debrief: Are you faster in the dark?

readinessQuestions.q: If you used a tool, you should:
choices: Leave it where it is convenient
Clean/inspect per SOP and return it to its home
readinessQuestions.why: The next alarm is the test.

readinessQuestions.q: Not knowing the rig after weeks on it is:
Opening every compartment at a scene:
choices: Should be based on the assignment — know what you need and where it lives

skills.title: Portable Radio and Mayday Format
skills.summary: Turn it on, get the right channel, talk short, and know the Mayday format before you need it.
skills.whyItMatters: A probationary firefighter with a dead radio is invisible. A probationary firefighter who cannot call a Mayday is in extra danger.
learningPoints: Battery, channel, volume, emergency button — every shift.
Listen before you talk.
Practice the Mayday on a training channel.
Know your riding name (Engine 4 nozzle, etc.).

terminology.meaning: Radio emergency feature — know what it actually does on YOUR radios.

safetyNotes: Do not test Mayday on a live dispatch channel.
If the radio is not yours, do not change everyone else’s scan list as a joke.

drill.objective: Demonstrate radio ready-check, a short routine message, and a correct Mayday on a training talkgroup.
drill.equipment: Training radio or a taped-out radio with a timer, Mayday card.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Point to power, channel, mic, emergency button. Recite Mayday format.
debrief: What is your unit/assignment name?

15.title: 15-minute reps
15.instructions: Five Maydays from different locations. Officer answers as command.
debrief: Did command know where you were?

30.title: 30-minute scenario
30.instructions: Search drill ends in lost-exit. Call it, then follow the company self-rescue talk-through.
commonMistakes: Waiting for permission to be in trouble
debrief: When would you have called sooner?

readinessQuestions.q: A portable radio at the start of the shift should be:
choices: On, correct channel, charged, emergency feature understood
Turned off so it does not bother you

readinessQuestions.q: Mayday practice belongs on:
choices: A training channel per department rules
readinessQuestions.why: Do not create a real emergency.

readinessQuestions.q: If you are lost, you should:
choices: Stay quiet to avoid looking bad
Call a Mayday per SOP — early
Wait for the bottle to empty

skills.title: Hydrant Connection
skills.summary: Make the hydrant the way THIS company makes it: adapters, slow open, kinks dressed, a real ‘water available’ report.
skills.whyItMatters: If the hydrant person fails, the whole engine fails. Probation often owns this job.
learningPoints: Know the kit: wrench, gate, adapter, steamer cap.
The operator needs water at the pump, not a heroic pose at the plug.
Traffic will try to kill you. Be visible.
If it is dry or broken, say so immediately.
beforeYouDo: Watch one catch, then do the next with coaching.

terminology.meaning: Large hydrant outlet commonly used for LDH.

safetyNotes: Charging LDH. Street traffic. Do not straddle hose.

seeResources.label: Hydrant Operations (engineer)
seeResources.note: What the operator is watching while you work.

drill.objective: Complete a department hydrant catch and a meaningful water-available report, then dress the supply line.
drill.equipment: Hydrant kit, supply hose, engine or prop, vest, PPE.
drill.setup: Training hydrant if needed. Agree on radio words with the operator.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Lay out the kit in order. Name the slow-open rule.
debrief: What if the cap is stuck?

15.title: 15-minute catch
15.instructions: Make it, open on command, kink check, report.
debrief: Did the panel actually have water?

30.title: 30-minute engine support
30.instructions: Hydrant plus first line pull, then a full reset of both.
debrief: Can you do this in the rain at night?

readinessQuestions.q: Your report at the hydrant should mean:
choices: The operator has a usable supply at the pump — or you are telling them they do not

readinessQuestions.q: A dry hydrant is:
choices: An immediate radio problem for the operator/officer
Always the next hydrant’s issue later

skills.title: Ground Ladder Basics
skills.summary: Carry, heel, raise, and lock a ladder for a simple objective without hitting wires.
skills.whyItMatters: You will be the heel person. If you cannot heel, the tip person is in trouble.
learningPoints: Look up for wires every time.
Know which ladders are on THIS truck.
Locks and footing before anyone climbs.
Throwing ladders as a personality is how people get hurt.

terminology.meaning: Footing the base so the ladder can be raised and climbed.

safetyNotes: Overhead power. Unstable footing. Do not over-climb.

drill.objective: Select, carry, raise, lock, climb to a mark, and recover one department ground ladder.
drill.setup: Clear overhead hazards. Officer names the objective.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Match three jobs to three sticks on the rig.
debrief: Wires?

15.title: 15-minute raise
15.instructions: One clean raise and climb. Heel work scored.
debrief: Could a victim use this?

30.title: 30-minute two objectives
30.instructions: Window and a second-story egress. Recover both.
commonMistakes: Leaving a ladder as a trap
debrief: What would you ask the officer next time?

readinessQuestions.q: Before the ladder goes up, look for:
Your usual probationary job on a raise is often:
choices: Heel / footing and locking as trained
readinessQuestions.why: Be the best heel person they have.

readinessQuestions.q: Climbing before it is locked/footed:

officialSources.label: National Fire Academy

skills.title: Post-Call Reset
skills.summary: After the run: people, air, hose, tools, and a ready apparatus — before anyone sits down for a hero sandwich.
skills.whyItMatters: The next tones will not wait for your recap. Probationary firefighters who reset without being asked get trusted.
learningPoints: SCBA/cylinders first if you used air.
Hose and tools back to a deployable state.
Fuel, water tank, and warning lights as the engineer directs.
If something broke or went missing, say it before the next dispatch.
Rehab and decon still count as part of reset.
beforeYouDo: Who signs the rig back in service.

terminology.meaning: Returning crew and apparatus to response-ready.

safetyNotes: Do not rush into traffic to pick up hose without a spotter.
Contaminated PPE follows decon rules even when you are tired.

practiceResources.label: Firefighter Wellness
practiceResources.note: You are part of the reset.

drill.objective: After a mock run, complete a reset checklist: air, hose, tools, personnel, and a defect report.
drill.equipment: Apparatus, used (training) hose, spare cylinder as policy allows, checklist.
drill.setup: Seed a missing tool and an empty cylinder.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: List the order your company wants: people/air vs hose vs water.
debrief: Who tells dispatch we are available?

15.title: 15-minute reset
15.instructions: Mock call then reset against the clock without skipping defects.
debrief: Are we actually in service?

30.title: 30-minute dirty-fire reset
30.instructions: Include a decon/PPE step and a rehab drink. Do not skip cancer/CO habits because it was ‘just training.’
debrief: What would we do at 0330?

readinessQuestions.q: The best time to mention a missing tool is:
readinessQuestions.why: The next fire needs that tool.

readinessQuestions.q: Used SCBA cylinders:
choices: Follow department change/fill rules as part of reset
Stay on your back in the kitchen

readinessQuestions.q: Reset includes:
choices: Crew, air, hose, tools, apparatus, and problems found

skills.title: Company Life and Feedback
skills.summary: Be on time, ask for one correction, take it without drama, and keep a private learning log — no patient identifiers.
skills.whyItMatters: Skill without coachability still fails probation. Coachability without skill fails the fire.
learningPoints: Show up ready: sleep, gear, attitude.
Ask ‘what should I do better on the next one?’ after ordinary calls.
Write it down. You will forget.
The officer is not your enemy. The street is.
Do not put HIPPA/PHI or crew gossip in FireOpsSim.
beforeYouDo: A notebook or My Career log with no names of patients/victims.

terminology.meaning: The person whose standard you are actually being measured against.

safetyNotes: Harassment and unsafe orders have reporting paths — coachability does not mean accepting abuse or illegal acts.
Fatigue is a safety issue. Say when you are not safe to work.

drill.objective: After a drill or shift, ask for one keep and one improve, write it in a de-identified log, and pick tomorrow’s 15-minute skill.
drill.equipment: Notebook or My Career, a willing officer/FTO, a 15-minute skill already on FireOpsSim.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Write the question you will actually ask: keep + improve.
debrief: When will you ask — not in front of a customer?

15.title: 15-minute loop
15.instructions: Do a skill, ask, log, schedule the next rep.
debrief: What is tomorrow’s skill?

30.title: 30-minute week plan
30.instructions: Pick three probation skills for the next three shifts and put them on a card. Share with the officer.
debrief: Does this match the task book they actually use?

readinessQuestions.q: The most useful question after a routine call is:
choices: What should I repeat and what should I change next time?
readinessQuestions.why: Ordinary calls are where you get calibrated.

readinessQuestions.q: Patient names and addresses belong in:
choices: Official department/EMS records only — never in FireOpsSim

readinessQuestions.q: If an order is unsafe or illegal:
choices: Use department reporting/safety paths — you are not required to get killed to pass probation
readinessQuestions.why: There is a line. Know it.
